themes.name: Everforest
themes.description: Green-based, warm, soft-contrast theme designed to be easy on the eyes (medium contrast).
themes.notes: sainnhe/everforest ships no kitty/alacritty file; ANSI values come from the Vim scheme's own terminal mapping (colors/everforest.vim 'Terminal' section: black=bg3 (dark) / fg (light), white=fg (dark) / bg3 (light), bright = normal) with the medium palette in autoload/everforest.vim. Selection=bg_visual. Cursor is NOT defined by the theme (Cursor uses 'reverse' / terminal default) - cursor=foreground is our derivation. UI: surface=bg1, border=bg4 (VertSplit fg), muted=grey1, accent=green.

themes.name: Everforest Hard
themes.description: Everforest with hard contrast: the same green forest palette on a deeper background.
themes.notes: Source: sainnhe/everforest at the same commit as the everforest entry, hard palette in autoload/everforest.vim (g:everforest_background='hard'). Only the background shades change with contrast: background=bg0, selection=bg_visual, ANSI black (dark) / white (light) = bg3, surface=bg1, border=bg4. Foreground and accent colors are shared by all contrasts, so the rest of the ANSI mapping, cursor=foreground (our derivation), muted=grey1 and accent=green equal the everforest entry.

themes.name: Everforest Soft
themes.description: Everforest with soft contrast: the same green forest palette on a softer background.
themes.notes: Source: sainnhe/everforest at the same commit as the everforest entry, soft palette in autoload/everforest.vim (g:everforest_background='soft'). Only the background shades change with contrast: background=bg0, selection=bg_visual, ANSI black (dark) / white (light) = bg3, surface=bg1, border=bg4. themes.name: Gruvbox
themes.description: Retro groove color scheme with warm, earthy tones (medium contrast).
themes.copyright: No LICENSE file in morhetz/gruvbox: README.md 'License' section says MIT/X11 and package.json says license MIT, author 'Pavel Pertsev <morhetz@gmail.com>'. No copyright line exists.
themes.notes: ANSI from gruvbox.vim's own Neovim terminal mapping (g:terminal_color_0..15), medium contrast. Dark matches gruvbox-contrib xresources exactly; light differs only in color0: xresources has #fdf4c1 (an older light0), vim uses bg0=#fbf1c7 (used here). gruvbox-contrib has no license. Cursor: theme uses 'inverse' (no explicit color) - cursor=foreground is our derivation. Selection=Visual bg (bg3). UI: surface=bg1, border=bg3 (VertSplit), muted=gray, accent=orange (hls_cursor default; accent choice is ours).

themes.name: Gruvbox Hard

themes.name: Solarized
themes.description: Precision sixteen-color palette with selective contrast, for dark and light backgrounds.
themes.notes: Hex values are the sRGB values from the README 'SOLARIZED HEX / 16/8 TERMCOL' table (ANSI slot per color from that table; same 16 for dark and light). The official .itermcolors files store calibrated (non-sRGB) floats that convert to different hex (e.g. #001e27), so they were used only for roles: bg=Ansi8/base03 (dark) or Ansi15/base3 (light), fg=cursor=base0 (dark) / base00 (light), selection=base02 (dark) / base2 (light). UI: surface=base02/base2 (background highlights), border and muted=base01 (dark) / base1 (light) (comments), accent=blue (our choice).

themes.name: GitHub
themes.description: GitHub's default dark and light themes.
themes.notes: Values from the GitHub Primer color tokens (primer/primitives 7.15.6) that github-nvim-theme vendors in lua/github-theme/palette/primitives/ (the file embeds primer's MIT license, 'Copyright (c) 2018 GitHub Inc.'). ANSI = Primer's top-level 'ansi' tokens (black..white, then the *Bright ones), GitHub's own terminal colors (the theme's nvim palette derives slightly different terminal colors from the scales; Primer's are used). background=canvas.default, foreground=fg.default, cursor=codemirror.cursor, selection=codemirror.selectionBg alpha-composited over the background (dark rgba(56,139,253,0.4) over canvas.default -> #1e4273; light rgba(84,174,255,0.4) over canvas.default -> #bbdfff). UI: surface=canvas.subtle, border=border.default, muted=fg.muted, accent=accent.fg. These are the primitives of github_dark_default / github_light_default (GitHub's current default themes), not the older github_dark / github_light palettes.

themes.name: Ayu
themes.description: Simple, bright-accented theme: Ayu Dark and Ayu Light.
themes.notes: Source: ayu-theme/vscode-ayu (MIT, the VS Code port in the ayu-theme organization), whose committed ayu-*.json files are generated from ayu-theme/ayu-colors; ayu-colors itself only stores OKLCH formulas, so the resolved hex values are read from the port. Terminal: terminal.background, terminal.foreground and terminal.ansi*. cursor=editorCursor.foreground (no terminalCursor key). selection=editor.selectionBackground alpha-composited over terminal.background (dark #3388ff40 -> #172e51; light #035bd626 -> #d3e1f5). UI: surface=titleBar.activeBackground, border=panel.border (light: #6b7d8f1f alpha-composited over the background -> #e7eaed), muted=foreground (ayu's UI text color), accent=focusBorder (ayu's accent).

UI: surface=titleBar.activeBackground, border=panel.border, muted=foreground (ayu's UI text color), accent=focusBorder (ayu's accent).

themes.name: One
themes.description: Atom's One Dark and One Light, the classic editor pair.
themes.notes: Terminal values from olimorris/onedarkpro.nvim (MIT) extras/ghostty/onedarkpro_onedark and onedarkpro_onelight: the ghostty files are the only ones that define cursor and selection (the kitty files say 'cursor none'; the alacritty files use different bright blacks). UI: muted=comment and accent=blue from onedarkpro lua/onedarkpro/themes/*.lua; onedarkpro computes its surface shades at runtime (darken/blend), so surface=syntax_cursor (StatusLine bg) and border=special_grey come from rakr/vim-one colors/one.vim (MIT, 'Copyright (c) 2016 Ramzi Akremi'), an Atom One port with explicit hex for both variants.

themes.name: Night Owl
themes.description: Night Owl for night owls, with the Light Owl daytime variant.
themes.notes: ANSI from the themes' own terminal.ansi* keys. Light Owl: background/foreground=terminal.background/terminal.foreground, selection=editor.selectionBackground (no terminal.selectionBackground key). Night Owl has no terminal.background/foreground keys, so VS Code's fallbacks are used: background=panel.background (= editor.background), foreground=foreground (= editor.foreground); selection=terminal.selectionBackground #1b90dd4d alpha-composited over the background -> #093b5e. cursor=editorCursor.foreground in both (no terminalCursor.foreground key). UI dark: surface=tab.inactiveBackground (the title bar and side bar share the editor background), border=statusBar.border, muted=Comment token color, accent=button.hoverBackground (the signature purple; button.background is the same color at 80% alpha). UI light: surface=titleBar.activeBackground, border=panel.border, muted=Comment token color, accent=button.background.
